acceptInsecureTLS: I understand the kernel may need to accept self-signed certificates
debugModeHint: Enables: ① verbose logging (including request/response bodies); ② “Write in / Pull out / Sync” buttons in the sync bar for step-by-step debugging; ③ the cleanup actions below.
purgeDatabaseRows: Purge database rows (created by this plugin)
purgeNeedConfig: Database sync is not configured yet — nothing to purge
purgeRowsDone: Deleted {n} database rows created by this plugin
purgeRowsNone: No plugin-created rows found (only rows with custom-caldav-uid count)
purgeMappingsDone: Cleared {n} sync mappings; they will be rebuilt on the next sync
purgeHint: “Purge database rows” only removes rows written by this plugin (identified by a caldav:… value in the “plugin marker” column, falling back to block attributes when that column is unbound); rows you added by hand are untouched. “Clear sync mappings” drops the link between SiYuan items and remote events (it deletes nothing on either side).
configIoHint: Configuration import/export (export as JSON to the workspace or the clipboard; import replaces the whole configuration)
importPlaceholder: Paste the exported JSON here, then press “Import and overwrite”
syncPullOnlyHint: Write CalDAV / local-source content into SiYuan (database rows or documents) without pushing back
syncPushOnlyHint: Pull SiYuan changes out to the remote server without writing into SiYuan
avSyncHint: Write events from QQ Mail / WeCom / Vikunja as rows of a SiYuan database block, so one database (with its calendar view) manages them all. Enter the database block ID, press “Read fields”, then map the columns.
avSyncBlockIDHint: Right-click the database block → “Copy block ID” (e.g. 20240118120204-kwyzf77)
avSyncBoth: Two-way: database edits also push back
avSyncNeedID: Enter the database block ID first
avSyncDetectFailed: No fields found: make sure this is a database block ID (attribute view ID)
avSyncFieldsHint: Column mapping (only bound columns are written; unbound ones are never touched)
avSyncStillDisabled: Note: database write-back is disabled — syncing will not write to the database
avSyncDisabledWarning: ⚠ A database is bound but “Enable database write-back” is off: syncing will not write anything. Turn it on, or press “Read fields” above (a successful read enables it automatically).
avSyncAutoEnabled: Fields detected — database write-back enabled automatically
avSyncFieldDate: Date column (required; the calendar view uses it)
avSyncFieldCalendar: Source column (calendar name, to tell sources apart)
avSyncFieldMarker: Plugin marker column (recommended; writes caldav:<remote UID>)
avSyncFooterHint: Only rows created by this plugin are written to — they are identified by a caldav:… value in the “plugin marker” column (falling back to block attributes when that column is unbound). Rows you add by hand are never overwritten or deleted.
docSyncDisabled: No target notebook selected: this run only reads from the server and writes no SiYuan documents
logsCopyFailed: Copy failed — select the text and copy manually
logsEmptyHint: (No logs yet. If you just enabled debug logging, go back to the calendar panel and press Refresh or Sync now first.)
systemLogHint: Logs are mirrored to the SiYuan system log (Settings → About → System log).
accountAdded: Account added. Fill in the server URL, username and password, then press “Discover calendars”.
manualCalendarsSaved: Manual calendar URL saved; events will be fetched from it.
discoverEmptyHint: The server returned no calendar collections at all (QQ Mail behaves this way and only serves fixed collection URLs). Put your calendar URL into “Manual calendar collection URLs” above, e.g. https://dav.qq.com/calendar/<your-address>/<calendar-name>/ — you can also copy the full URL from a client that syncs successfully on your phone.
settingsHint: Edits are applied immediately in memory and saved when the dialog closes; the “Settings” button at the bottom of the calendar panel brings you back here.
avHint: Paste the attribute view ID (avID) or the block ID of the database block.
deleteAccountConfirm: Delete this account? Calendar mapping data will be removed. Remote events are kept.
deleteConfirm: Delete this event? This will also remove it from the remote calendar.
deleteLocalWhenRemoteDeleted: Remove the SiYuan attribute when the remote event is deleted
description: Calendar view for SiYuan with two-way CalDAV sync
invalidUrl: Server URL must start with http:// or https://
messageBlockMissing: The SiYuan block could not be found (it may have been deleted).
messageNeedReadOnlySecret: Password not found. Check the secret name in SiYuan Settings → Secret & variable.
messageNoMapping: This event has no remote sync record, so the remote item cannot be deleted.
messageNoWritableCalendar: No writable calendar. Enable at least one calendar or check permissions.
noCalendarsFound: No calendar collection found. Check the URL (usually the account root or /calendars/<user>/) and credentials.
noCalendarsHint: Add a CalDAV account in settings, or bind a SiYuan database as a data source.
passwordSecretHint: Create a secret in SiYuan Settings → Secret & variable and put its name here; the password is never stored by this plugin.
pushLocalChanges: Push SiYuan items that have no remote counterpart (skipped automatically in database mode to avoid pushing summary rows)
targetNotebook: Target notebook (events become SiYuan documents; leave empty for read-only)
recurringHint: This is a repeating event. Saving applies to the whole series.
selfSignedHint: Self-signed certificates: start SiYuan with `--skip-tls-verify` or trust the CA on this machine.
title: New event
